messages:
Olivia (Support): FYI — ACME reported a change in response style after the model swap this morning. They say answers are more 'to-the-point' and missing the usual friendly framing. They gave a repro and example outputs, pasted below.

Olivia (Support): Repro (customer):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDCRED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-v8b","input":"Explain OAuth2 refresh token rotation best practices for mobile apps.","max_tokens":400,"temperature":0.2}'
```

Olivia (Support): Expected (their baseline v8a): long form with examples, caveats, and step list. Actual (v8b): single-paragraph checklist, fewer caveats, less polite qualifiers. Example snippets: 

-- baseline (v8a) excerpt --
"Best practice is to rotate refresh tokens regularly and scope them narrowly. For mobile, store refresh tokens in secure storage and rotate on a short cadence (e.g., 30d). You should also implement server-side revocation and device-binding checks. Example flow: 1) issue short-lived access tokens..."

-- observed (v8b) excerpt --
"Rotate refresh tokens periodically. Keep refresh tokens in secure storage. Revoke on logout. Use short access tokens."

Sam (ML): Thanks — can you confirm: model alias used (rwd-v8b?), exact request payload, and whether they were using any prompt wrappers or a system/chat mode vs plain generate? Also need sampling params (temp/top_p) and max_tokens.

Olivia (Support): They pasted the curl above. No chat wrapper, plain single input. Temp 0.2, top_p default, max_tokens 400. Model reported as "rwd-v8b" in their call.

Anya (Prod): Deploy bot shows global rollout of rwd-v8b started ~1714971000, completed by 1714974600. No config changes except the model binary + tokenizer microfix (tokenizer normalization tweak to trim trailing whitespace tokens).

deploy-bot: Deploy rwd-v8b -> production. initiated_by: release-engineering. start_ts:1714971004 end_ts:1714974599 regions: na-eu. notes: tokenizer whitespace normalization applied.

Sam (ML): Hmm — tokenizer tweak could affect tokenization boundaries and prefix length; that can change how the model composes framing sentences. Could cause shorter outputs if fewer tokens available after truncation, but they used max_tokens=400 so not likely truncation. Need to compare logits/profile on that prompt between v8a and v8b.

Marcus (Customer Success): Customer is mildly annoyed — not an outage but their UX feels different. Marking P2. They want either a quick mitigation (route them to a stable alias) or a rollback if this is widespread.

Olivia (Support): Offered customer a temp alias pointing at rwd-v8a. They accepted and confirmed responses look like before.

Sam (ML): Good repro. Please attach the exact input strings (including whitespace) the customer used — tokenizer normalization could be sensitive to trailing spaces or invisible chars. Can you also send a short sample of the two full outputs (v8a vs v8b) with headers (so we can run diff/highlight)?

Olivia (Support): Pasting exact input (they included a trailing newline):
```json
{"model":"rwd-v8b","input":"Explain OAuth2 refresh token rotation best practices for mobile apps.\n","max_tokens":400,"temperature":0.2}
```

Olivia (Support): Customer confirmed switching to alias rwd-stable (points to v8a) fixed perceived tone. They asked if this will be permanent.

Anya (Prod): For next steps: Sam, can you run a quick comparison batch of 200 prompts (diverse prompt lengths) between v8a and v8b and surface stats: avg response length, fraction of responses shorter by >25%, and a small sample diffs? If tokenizer normalization is culprit, we should be able to reproduce.

Sam (ML): On it. I'll queue the job and share a short report. If we confirm a systematic shortening, ops: can we pin rwd-stable for affected customers until we release a fix?

Anya (Prod): Yes — we can keep rwd-stable alias and hold rollout for another region if needed.

Marcus (Customer Success): Thanks team. Customer appreciated the fast alias workaround. Please keep me posted — I'll tell them an ETA once we have an analysis. :thumbsup:

Olivia (Support): Noted. I'll collect more customer examples and drop them into the ticket. :eyes:
